high_level_description: Strictly non-photographic, wordless Tongan ngatu composition: six women, one papa and one continuous barkcloth are rendered entirely as flat koka and tongo pigment motifs, each woman working a contiguous kupesi section that joins one uninterrupted whole; cream bark, reddish brown and black, no gradients, realistic depth, writing or arrows.

compositional_deconstruction.background: One uninterrupted cream bark field fills the frame. Broad reddish-brown and black kupesi borders enclose a single central working register, while smaller stepped diamonds, crossing curves, paired leaves, and nested chevrons repeat along the edges. Every form remains flat and integrated into the same surface, without sky, architectural room, horizon, realistic floor, receding perspective, royal device, national emblem, church symbol, inscription, letter, numeral, caption, arrow, interface, badge, throne, ranked seat, or tourist display.

elements.desc: One long low papa kokaʻanga crosses the central register with six adjacent kupesi relief panels beneath a single continuous sheet of cream barkcloth. Each panel carries distinct bands of stepped diamonds, crossing curves, paired leaves, and nested chevrons; their aligned borders join into one uninterrupted reddish-brown and black composition that curls gently at the bottom edge.

First Tongan ngatu maker seated at the upper-left side, dark-brown skin, black hair in a low bun, plain rust blouse, deep-brown wrap skirt, and bare feet. She presses a folded koka pigment pad over the first kupesi section with both hands, keeping her work within that contiguous area and looking down attentively.

Second Tongan ngatu maker seated along the left side, medium-brown skin, shoulder-length wavy black hair, cream blouse, dark rust wrap skirt, and bare feet. She rubs the second kupesi section with a compact fiber pad, aligning its boundary with the completed first band while neither reaching across the table nor directing another maker.

Third Tongan ngatu maker seated at the lower-left side, dark-brown skin, short coiled black hair, muted ochre blouse, black-brown wrap skirt, and bare feet. She strengthens black tongo details within the third contiguous section using a narrow pandanus brush, leaving the neighboring relief patterns and other women’s tools untouched.

Fourth Tongan ngatu maker seated opposite the first woman, medium-brown skin, long black hair braided down her back, dark-brown blouse, cream wrap skirt, and bare feet. She holds the cloth steady over the fourth kupesi while applying reddish-brown pigment evenly, matching the shared outer border without copying the internal motif of another section.

Fifth Tongan ngatu maker seated along the right side, dark-brown skin, black hair wrapped in a plain cream cloth, rust blouse, charcoal wrap skirt, and bare feet. She rubs the fifth kupesi with both hands, joining its border precisely to the adjacent work while maintaining a distinct nested-chevron interior and carrying no supervisory object.

Sixth Tongan ngatu maker seated near the lower-right end, medium-brown skin, straight black hair tied low, cream blouse, reddish-brown wrap skirt, and bare feet. She paints the final black accents on the sixth section as the continuous completed ngatu curls beneath the papa, with no separate output, prize mark, signature panel, or central leader.
